task.title: Complete tasks through an explicit workflow-phase turn
task.objective: Complete issue https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/754 with a caller-owned phase-assisted completion that preserves the final response as Attempt evidence and exact task output.
acceptance_criteria: Reject invalid task, Attempt, session, and phase state before provider effects.
Atomically persist valid assistant content with matching Attempt evidence before completion.
Use the exact response as task output without classifying it as Verification.
Preserve the response prefix and report authoritative state when a terminal race wins.

attempts.diagnostic: The focused test failed to compile because complete_workflow_phase_task_turn did not exist.
attempts.patch: Added success, deterministic preflight, provider-failure, and terminal-race tests.

attempts.diagnostic: Existing response validation, atomic assistant/Attempt persistence, and task completion already defined the required authority boundaries.
attempts.patch: Reused those boundaries after explicit phase resolution and retained assistant turn, Attempt, then completion ordering.

attempts.diagnostic: Substantive review found that success and terminal-race tests counted transcript turns without proving the exact preserved assistant content.
attempts.patch: Asserted the exact phase response in both durable transcript paths, reran verification, and held merge until the exact fix head received review capacity.

outcome.summary: Callers can explicitly complete an active associated task after a selected phase response, preserving exact Attempt and output evidence without granting the model workflow or verification authority.

verification.command: nix develop --command cargo test -p vela-kernel --test workflow_phase_runtime

lessons: Provider output may be exact task output and Attempt evidence without becoming independent Verification.
Terminal intent remains caller-owned even when the runtime owns ordered persistence.
Race tests should assert exact preserved content, not only event or turn counts.
A review fix is not merge-ready while its incremental review is rate limited.
